commentary_segments.text: Such integrating or dualslope ADC has many advantages. The result is independent of the actual values of the resistor R and capacitor 1 C . As long as the opamp 1 has sufficient gain, it does not affect the result. The linearity is high and so is the resolution. The circuitry is actually fairly simple. Only opamps are used, an RC circuit and some switches. The converter is fairly slow, however. For a large input voltage, such as V itself, the counter has to count up over 2N ref clock pulses and also down over as many pulses. The conversion time is thus quite long. For slow digital voltmeters, this is an excellent solution. This is especially true if the hum of the 50 Hz mains (60 Hz in USA) is synchronized by the clock. In this way the effect of the hum is cancelled. At the input of an oscilloscope, higher speeds are required however, and less resolution.
